cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice acceptance speech. I taught you to project, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me to order pizza when I was eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And tonight an auditorium heard you. Progress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote the speech myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finally applying my lesson about not asking for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely portrait. You're finally getting the shadows I tried to teach you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My new teacher told me to stop mixing everything with black.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You're ready to move beyond my introductory method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She made me throw out your paint set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You used to be far too sentimental. I was beginning to worry I'd never get you past that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've spent hours on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Mum's coming for lunch. Is this spoon clean enough for her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spoon's fine. You haven't cleaned the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. She checks cutlery. Could you check the forks while I finish this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've told her to bring rubber gloves and help you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a guest towel. Can you help me choose one without a faded stripe?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.text: Good. You're ready to move beyond my introductory method.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Sit down, love. You've been on the ward all night. I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's there a bucket by my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Just catching a drip. Take the sofa; I've made you a tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay here. I'll bring your duvet down; upstairs needs a little drying before I put your bed back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice acceptance speech. I taught you to project, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me to order pizza when I was eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And tonight an auditorium heard you. Progress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote the speech myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finally applying my lesson about not asking for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely portrait. You're finally getting the shadows I tried to teach you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My new teacher told me to stop mixing everything with black.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You're ready to move beyond my introductory method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She made me throw out your paint set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You used to be far too sentimental. I was beginning to worry I'd never get you past that.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?
